{{Short description|Estonian mathematician (1946–2007)}}

'''Taivo Arak''' (2 November 1946, [[Tallinn]] – 17 October 2007, [[Stockholm]]) was an Estonian mathematician, specializing in probability theory.

==Biography==
In 1969 he graduated from [[St. Petersburg State University|Leningrad State University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.spbu.ru/Euler/|title=Выдающиеся матмеховцы (Outstanding mathematicians)|publisher=math.spbu.ru}}</ref> There he received in 1972 his Russian candidate degree (Ph.D.) under [[Ildar Abdulovich Ibragimov|I. A. Ibragimov]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=51579}}</ref>

In 1983 Arak defended his dissertation for his [[Doktor nauk|Russian doctorate]] (higher doctoral degree similar to [[habilitation]]).

From 1972 to 1981 he worked at the [[Tallinn University of Technology]]. From 1981 he worked at the Institute of Cybernetics of the Academy of Sciences of the Estonian SSR.<ref>[http://interpretive.ru/dictionary/1019303/word/arak-taivo-viktorovich Арак, Тайво Викторович (Arak, Taivo Viktorovich)— Биографическая энциклопедия (Biographical Encyclopedia)]</ref> In 1986 he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Berkeley, California]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Arak, Taivo|chapter=A class of Markov fields with finite range|title=Proc. Intern. Congress of Mathematicians, Berkeley|pages=994–999|year=1986}}</ref>

Most of his research dealt with the theory of probability.

==Awards==
* {{ill|Markov Prize|ru|Премия Маркова}} (1983) - for the series of papers "Равномерные предельные теоремы для сумм независимых случайных величин" (Uniform limit theorems for sums of independent random variables).
